fixture.note: read-only; CodeGraph and edit probes ran on a scratch copy

groundTruth: TypeScript language service getDefinitionAtPosition at every call/new callee in all fixture files; only definitions that are in-project tracked declarations (top-level function/class/method/interface member/fn-typed property/variable) count

strataDefinition.alias: callee bound by a non-relative import resolved through tsconfig paths
strataDefinition.barrel: callee bound by an import whose module is not the defining file (>=1 re-export hop)
strataDefinition.dynamic: element access, optional call, or call through an interface/type member

treeSitter.role: syntax only + our name/import/re-export resolver (unique method name, no types)

incrementalUpdateMs.note: reparse + re-extract one file + re-resolve all calls

scipTypescript.role: type-checker symbols via SCIP; call edges = SCIP references at call-expression callees found by tree-sitter

incrementalUpdateMs.note: no incremental mode: the whole project is re-indexed

codegraph.role: BENCHMARK ONLY (bundled runtime, own schema); not a Mole dependency

fullIndexMs.note: CLI wall time incl. process start

incrementalUpdateMs.note: CLI `sync` wall time incl. process start

caveats: Ground truth is the TS language service, so the Compiler API engine (same checker) is partly circular; SCIP also uses the TS checker. Tree-sitter and CodeGraph are the independent measurements.
Matching key is call line + target; same-line same-target calls count once (slightly generous).
SCIP call sites come from the tree-sitter extractor, so SCIP recall inherits its site detection.
Incremental time = one probe file, edit at end of file, reuses parsed files by mtime; dependents are not re-resolved.
Strata are decided from the call-site syntax and the language-service definition, so a few barrel/alias sites could fall into a neighbouring stratum.
Matching key is call line + target file + target leaf name; two calls to the same name on one line count once.

Only 15 barrel call sites exist in the fixture (all sampled); alias sites are ~all calls into the ambient `declare module '@hermes/ink'` in src/types/hermes-ink.d.ts. Both strata are small/narrow, so per-stratum recall there is weak evidence.
recallStatic = every stratum except dynamic (alias + barrel + method + static); this is the figure the task stop row (<0.9) refers to.

The tree-sitter engine is our own resolver (imports, re-exports, tsconfig paths, ambient modules, unique-method-name), not an off-the-shelf tool; a smarter resolver would score higher but would be reimplementing the type checker.
Times are wall-clock on one Apple-silicon Mac, node v22.21.0, not a controlled benchmark.

nodeRuntime.indexerNeeds: Node >=22.5 for node:sqlite (flag-free from 22.13); typescript itself needs Node >=14.17
nodeRuntime.vscodeExtensionHost: Node 22.15.1 since VS Code 1.101 (May 2025, Electron 35); Node 20 before that. Source: https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_101
nodeRuntime.consequence: In-process node:sqlite works in VS Code >=1.101. Older VS Code or forks still on Electron <35 need a fallback driver, or run the indexer in the planned M1 daemon (own Node) instead of the extension host. Forks (Cursor, Windsurf) not checked.

candidates.treeSitter: web-tree-sitter: unspecified; WASM, runs in any Node or a browser
candidates.scipTypescript: unspecified (CLI spawns its own process; no Node floor declared)

recommendation.decision: P2 stays PROPOSED until Raymond accepts
recommendation.engine: TypeScript Compiler API (packages/indexer) + SQLite via node:sqlite. Built, tested, 362 files indexed.
why: Best accuracy: precision 1, recall 1 on 215 sampled call sites incl. dynamic 100%. Circular by construction (ground truth is also TypeScript), so the independent evidence is SCIP 0.964 static recall and the tree-sitter/CodeGraph gaps.
Fast enough: full index 5833 ms (limit 5 min); 1-file update 97 ms vs 5318 ms for SCIP (no incremental mode) and 934 ms for CodeGraph.

Weighted by real call volume the gap on everyday calls is small (static recall 1 TS, 0.978 SCIP, 0.972 tree-sitter, 0.964 CodeGraph, because ~90% of call sites are plain static). The type-checker advantage is in the rare hard cases: dynamic dispatch (tree-sitter 0%, CodeGraph 2%) and aliases/barrels (tree-sitter barrel 27%).
Small + licensed: 22.8 MB, Apache-2.0, no native code.
It is what tsc and VS Code use, which matches the USER criterion (popular, industry-standard, job-relevant).
recommendation.scip: Not in v1 core: 94% recall / 0.979 precision is close, but it has no incremental mode and no call concept (needs a parser to find call sites). Keep as a CI/M6 import and the route to other languages (other SCIP indexers).
recommendation.treeSitter: Not for call edges: static recall 0.885, dynamic 0. Keep for fast structure/outline and non-TS languages: full parse 819 ms, 1-file 20 ms.
recommendation.codegraph: Reject as a dependency: 284.5 MB, static recall 0.733, alias 19/50, dynamic 1/50, own schema. Benchmark only, as planned.
